title: Chapter 4 Quiz 11
description: Traps in every question. Rows, columns, fields and files are easy to mix up.
topic: Difficult: tables, records and hidden errors
instructions: Chapter 4: Difficult: tables, records and hidden errors.
Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: This should read a matrix declared as [1..3][1..3]. One line is wrong. Find it and choose the fix.
questions.code:
Declare M [1..3][1..3] : ARRAY OF integer
For i From 1 To 3 Do
    For j From 1 To 4 Do
        Read(M[i][j])
    EndFor
EndFor
questions.explanation: The columns are numbered 1 to 3. Watch out: To 4 would read M[i][4], which does not exist.

questions.question:
How many times does the inner body run?
```
For i From 1 To 4 Do
    For j From i To 4 Do
        Display(M[i][j])
    EndFor
EndFor
```
questions.explanation: i = 1 gives 4 passes, i = 2 gives 3, i = 3 gives 2 and i = 4 gives 1: 10. Watch out: the inner loop starts at i, so it is not 4 × 4 = 16.

questions.question: Give the sum of each row and each column of the matrix [2 5 1 / 4 0 3 / 6 2 2].
questions.explanation: Row 1 = 2 + 5 + 1 = 8; row 3 = 6 + 2 + 2 = 10; column 1 = 2 + 4 + 6 = 12; column 2 = 5 + 0 + 2 = 7. Watch out: a row runs across, and a column runs down.

questions.question: In the matrix [2 5 1 / 4 0 3 / 6 2 2], which value is M[3][2]?
questions.explanation: M[3][2] is row 3, column 2: the value 2. Watch out: the first index is the row. M[2][3] would be 3.

questions.question: What does students[3].age mean?
options: The age of the third student
questions.explanation: The index picks the record, and the dot picks the field. Watch out: the index comes before the dot.

questions.question: This should read the name of each of 4 students stored in an array of records. One line is wrong. Find it and type the corrected line.
questions.code:
TYPE STUDENT = RECORD
    Name: string
    Average: real
END RECORD
Declare students [1..4] : ARRAY OF STUDENT
For i From 1 To 4 Do
    Read(students.Name[i])
EndFor
questions.explanation: We first pick the record with the index, then the field with the dot: students[i].Name. Watch out: students.Name[i] puts the index on the field, which is a string.

questions.question: This should find the largest value of a 3×3 matrix. One line has an error.
questions.code:
Let max ← M[1][1]
For i From 1 To 3 Do
    For j From 1 To 3 Do
        If M[i][j] < max Then
            max ← M[i][j]
        EndIf
    EndFor
EndFor
questions.explanation: We replace max when the new value is larger. Watch out: with < the code finds the smallest value.

questions.question: A record can store a string and a real number together.
questions.explanation: Fields can have different types. Watch out: an array could not mix a string and a real number.

questions.question: Which statement about reset and rewrite is true?
options: reset creates the file when it is missing
reset erases the old content of the file
rewrite creates the file or erases an old one
rewrite opens a file only for reading
questions.explanation: rewrite opens for writing, and erases an existing file. Watch out: reset opens an existing file for reading and erases nothing.

questions.question: A staff file stores 20 records, each with 3 fields. How many values does it hold?
questions.explanation: 20 × 3 = 60. Watch out: the values are multiplied, not added (23).

questions.assertion: A record can hold fields of different types.
questions.reason: All the cells of an array have the same type.
questions.explanation: Both are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion: it states what an array does, as a contrast. Watch out: the reason is true, yet it is about arrays, not about records.
